title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
abstract: arXiv:2611.19499v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions closer to the mean difference. translated_title: 探测与引导在语言模型内部及跨模型间是否偏好相同的方向？
translated_abstract: 语言模型隐藏状态中的某个方向可用于探测某个概念是否存在，或将模型引导至该概念。尽管探测方向常被复用于引导，但最能检测某个概念的方向未必是最能改变它的方向。我们在来自不同系列的三个指令微调模型中研究了这一区别。我们构建了一个单参数方向族，其范围从协方差调整判别式到均值差，并在固定副作用的情况下沿该方向族评估探测和加性引导（即将该方向添加到隐藏状态）。对于真实性和情感这两个概念，在所有模型中，最佳探测方向都不是最佳引导方向：引导始终偏好更接近均值差的方向。这种分离在层扫描中60个层-模型-概念组合中的59个上成立，并在所有六个模型-概念组合中均使用匹配的探测和引导文本进行验证。
tldr: 该研究揭示了语言模型中最优探测方向与最优引导方向并不相同——引导始终偏好更接近均值差的方向，且这一发现在不同模型系列和几乎所有层中均成立，表明探测与引导是本质上不同的任务。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that the direction best for probing whether a concept is present differs from the direction best for steering the model toward it, with steering consistently favoring directions closer to the mean difference across different model families and nearly all layers.
